verdict.rationale: Superpowers operates inside git worktrees, treats plan files/ledgers as durable state, and includes an explicit code-reviewer/review-fix loop that evaluates implementations against plans — giving natural versioning (git history) and review of generated work. However, there is no dedicated feature for versioning or rolling back the skills/automations themselves beyond git-based safety nets (e.g. refusing destructive worktree removal); rollback is implicit via git rather than a first-class capability. Missing for 10: explicit skill/automation version history, a dedicated rollback command or UI, and independent evidence of successful rollback use.
